title: AWX
description: AWX is the hands: every verb in infra-objectives executes through it. These are AWX's own metrics, scraped from OUTSIDE the cluster it runs in, so an outage shows as up == 0 rather than as missing data.

panels.title: AWX reachable
panels.description: The scrape runs from the PostgreSQL VM, outside the Kubernetes cluster AWX lives in. A 0 here is a measurement; if this panel is empty instead, the collector or Grafana is the problem, not AWX.

panels.title: Capacity remaining
panels.description: Summed across AWX instances. Jobs queue when this reaches zero — which looks like AWX being slow rather than AWX being full, and is the distinction this panel exists to make.

panels.title: Database connections
panels.description: AWX's own view of PostgreSQL. This is the level-3 metric that answers a level-1 question: it says the database is reachable FROM AWX, which is a different fact from the postgres VM being up — and the two diverge exactly when it matters.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: AWX control pods reporting capacity. south runs six; a drop means pods are gone or not heartbeating.

panels.title: Capacity per instance
panels.description: Per AWX pod. Pods come and go on redeploy, so gaps here are normal; all of them dropping at once is not.

panels.title: Database connections over time
panels.description: A climbing floor here, rather than a spike, is the shape that precedes AWX becoming unusable while every pod still reports healthy.

panels.title: Inventory of the estate, as AWX sees it
panels.description: Counts of the things this repo manages. Useful as a change detector: hosts or job templates moving when nobody deployed anything is worth a look.

panels.title: What this dashboard cannot tell you

options.content:
**Nothing about AWX's pods.** These are AWX's own application metrics, reported by AWX about itself. Pod restarts, evictions, image pulls and scheduling failures need `kube-state-metrics`, which must run inside the cluster — blocked on the `infra-observability` ServiceAccount.

**Nothing about PostgreSQL itself.** `awx_database_connections_total` is AWX's view of its database. Disk, bloat, locks and replication need `postgres_exporter` and a read-only `pg_monitor` role on that VM.

**Nothing when AWX is down.** If AWX cannot serve `/api/v2/metrics`, every panel here goes flat except `up`, which is precisely why the scrape runs from outside the cluster. Cross-check with the **Management plane** dashboard: if the PostgreSQL VM and the Kubernetes nodes are healthy while AWX is not, the fault is in the application layer.

**Nothing about whether a job did the right thing.** AWX reports that jobs ran, not that they were correct — a job template pointed at an empty inventory reports success. See rule 8 in `CLAUDE.md`.
